Your working tree is clean and the local git config is standard. The main thing to preserve is the ability to restore your repository and any SSH/auth setup. Here are the best options:

**Option 1: Push a backup branch to your backup host (simplest)**
```powershell
git remote add backup ssh://sam@localhost/path/to/backup/repo.git
git push backup main
git push backup --all  # backs up all branches/tags
```

**Option 2: Create a tarball backup to copy to backup host**
```powershell
tar -czf project-backup.tar.gz .git/
# then copy to backup host
```

**Option 3: Just verify SSH access works to backup host**
```powershell
ssh backup "echo 'Backup host is accessible'"
```

Which approach would you prefer? Most importantly — do you know the path to the git repository on your backup host (localhost), or do you need to set that up first?
